results.title: ServiceNow lays out path to $30 billion in annual subscription revenue as AI bets accelerate - Business Insider
results.content: # ServiceNow lays out path to $30 billion in annual subscription revenue as AI bets accelerate. * ServiceNow aims to double subscription revenue to $30 billion by 2030. * ServiceNow's Now Assist product surpassed $750 million in annual contract value, its CFO said. During a meeting with analysts, ServiceNow President and CFO Gina Mastantuono said the company is targeting more than $30 billion in subscription revenue by 2030, up from an expected $15.7 billion in 2026. On Monday, the CFO said its Now Assist product, a flagship AI offering, surpassed $600 million in annual contract value (ACV) in 2025 and has exceeded $750 million as of the first quarter of 2026. The company expects that figure to top $1.5 billion by the end of this year and account for more than 30% of total ACV by 2030. results.title: ESTEVE'S EXPANSION AND GROWTH IN EU AND USA ACCELERATES ITS TRANSFORMATION INTO A GLOBAL HEALTHCARE COMPANY - BioSpace
results.content: # ESTEVE’S EXPANSION AND GROWTH IN EU AND USA ACCELERATES ITS TRANSFORMATION INTO A GLOBAL HEALTHCARE COMPANY. * **New assets in both businesses – Pharma and CDMO – fuel double-digit growth in net revenues and EBITDA and prove strong strategy execution**. * **CDMO business grows with new assets in the USA, adding early development capabilities**. BARCELONA, Spain, May 4, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- ESTEVE today presented its 2025 results, highlighting a year of strong strategic execution, **double-digit growth** both in net revenues (+14%[1] vs 2024) and EBITDA (+19% vs 2024) and a deepened commitment to ESG social and environmental responsibility. Throughout 2025, ESTEVE continued to advance its long-term roadmap as a global healthcare company combining inorganic growth in its pharma business with the adding of **highly specialized medicines**. The company also strengthened its **CDMO business**, gaining wider early development capabilities with the purchase of a new business in the USA.

results.title: Vodafone to take control of VodafoneThree in £4.3bn buyout - Total Telecom
results.content: Posted by Harry Baldock | May 5, 2026 | 5G, M&A, COMPANY NEWS, Networks, News, UK. Vodafone has announced it will purchase CK Hutchison’s 49% stake in VodafoneThree for £4.3 billion, giving the UK-based mobile giant full control of the joint venture. Max Taylor will remain a CEO of the company and Vodafone will retain the use of the Three brand. CK Hutchison said the deal provided an “attractive” valuation, while Vodafone said deal will allow for continued simplification of operations, with the company aiming to achieve around £700 million in annual capex by the 2030 financial year.
